title: Permutation Construction Consistent with Existing Mappings
summary: Easy permutation construction is available on the domain, but extending it while preserving existing table mappings for use on new points remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Given a domain $X$ on which permutations are easy to construct and an existing table of mappings from a preservation set $T \subseteq X$ to its range $U$, how can one construct a new permutation on $X$ that agrees with every table mapping on $T$, thereby preserving the existing mappings while permitting the new permutation to be used on new points?

scope.domain: Combinatorial and structural questions about constructing permutations on special domains in symmetric cryptography.
assumptions: Permutations are easy to construct on the domain X.
parameters: X, the domain on which the permutation is constructed
T, the preservation set whose table mappings must be retained
U, the range of the existing table mappings
scope.unresolved_remainder: Construct a new permutation on X that agrees with every existing table mapping on T while remaining usable on new points.

citations.label: Cycle Slicer: An Algorithm for Building Permutations on Special Domains

progress.summary: The source presents this as a practical problem and explicitly recasts it as a theoretical question about constructing a permutation consistent with an existing table of mappings.
citation_labels: Sarah Miracle et al., Cycle Slicer: An Algorithm for Building Permutations on Special Domains
